stem: A client with an acutely swollen, painful native knee undergoes arthrocentesis. Synovial fluid has a very high white blood cell count with marked neutrophil predominance. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: The findings strongly raise concern for septic arthritis, but culture and the full clinical picture are needed because crystal arthritis can overlap
options.B: The findings alone confirm bacterial septic arthritis and exclude gout or pseudogout
options.C: The findings are most characteristic of noninflammatory osteoarthritis
options.D: The findings make joint infection unlikely, so synovial culture is unnecessary

rationale: NCBI StatPearls notes that a very high synovial WBC count with strong neutrophil predominance suggests a bacterial source, but similarly inflammatory counts can also occur with acute gout or pseudogout. Identification of a bacterial organism in synovial fluid confirms septic arthritis. Therefore A is the most accurate interpretation: the result requires urgent clinical attention but should not be treated as a stand-alone definitive diagnosis.
educational_objective: Interpret a markedly inflammatory, neutrophil-predominant synovial fluid result as highly concerning for septic arthritis while recognizing that culture and clinical context are required for confirmation.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; current NCBI pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Septic Arthritis > Evaluation > Laboratory Studies: synovial WBC >50,000 with 90% neutrophil predominance suggests bacterial source and identification of a bacterial organism confirms diagnosis; Arthritis > synovial fluid analysis: >50,000 cells/mm3 and/or >90% neutrophils raise suspicion for septic arthritis but can also occur with acute gout or pseudogout
source_claim_supported: Marked synovial leukocytosis with neutrophil predominance raises strong suspicion for septic arthritis but is not fully specific; organism identification in synovial fluid confirms infection.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — Laboratory Values and Diagnostic Tests: compare laboratory results with expected findings, recognize abnormal diagnostic findings, and determine the need for follow-up
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Diagnostic Tests / synovial fluid interpretation
correction_summary: Corrected the source item's implication that neutrophil-predominant synovial leukocytosis essentially identifies bacterial infection. The final item explicitly preserves the strong septic-arthritis concern while acknowledging overlap with crystal arthritis and the confirmatory role of culture.
audit_findings: A reflects both the high-risk interpretation and the known limitation of synovial cell counts. B is an overclaim because crystal arthritis can produce overlapping high leukocyte/neutrophil findings. C contradicts the inflammatory fluid pattern; osteoarthritis is generally noninflammatory. D is unsafe and contradicts the need for synovial culture in suspected septic arthritis. The item retains no unsupported claim that a single threshold is perfectly diagnostic and maps cleanly to NCSBN Reduction of Risk Potential laboratory/diagnostic interpretation.
